verdict.rationale: First-party docs say OpenClaw can run tool execution inside a sandbox backend to reduce blast radius, with documented modes, scopes, workspace access and images. The exec tool is bounded by whatever the selected host or sandbox filesystem permits, and hardened per-tenant container cells are available. The architecture page describes untrusted execution under deterministic policy, and node and computer-use control is capability- and permission-based. Community comments that the default security model amounts to 'running as root' are opinions rather than a documented sandbox failure, so they lower confidence but do not create a dispute. Missing for 10: detailed evidence of per-tool allow/deny policies or approval modes, clarity on whether sandboxing is on by default, and independent hands-on corroboration that the sandbox contains risky runs.
